question: A mother asks which local foods she can give her toddler to prevent iron deficiency. What should you recommend?

options.A: Cassava flakes (garri) soaked in plain cold water
options.B: Pure vegetable oil and polished white rice
options.C: White bread, refined sugar, and bottled juices
options.D: Lean meats, liver, beans, and dark green leafy vegetables

question: What is the primary shape of human kidneys?

options.A: Bean-shaped
options.B: Disc-shaped
options.C: Spherical
options.D: Crescent-shaped

explanation: Human kidneys have a characteristic bean shape and sit in the posterior abdominal wall. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h1)

question: If a patient has too much sodium in their blood, where does water naturally rush to?

options.A: Out of the blood vessels completely through the skin
options.B: From the interstitial spaces into the lymphatic system
options.C: From the extracellular space directly into the cells
options.D: From inside the cells into the extracellular space

question: Why is relying solely on clinical tradition dangerous in modern healthcare?

options.A: Patients always reject care based on historical habits
options.B: Traditions are often outdated and unsupported by current evidence
options.C: Traditions cost too much money to maintain in hospitals
options.D: Physicians refuse to follow traditional nursing methods

explanation: Habits passed down through generations of staff may be ineffective or even harmful compared to modern tested methods. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why would adult Ascaris worms sometimes wander out of the intestines into the liver ducts or pancreas?

options.A: Active hunting for food sources outside the intestinal tract
options.B: Attraction to high concentrations of oxygen in the liver
options.C: Disturbance from fever, illness, or sub-lethal anti-parasitic treatment
options.D: Normal biological necessity to complete their reproductive cycle

question: What usually happens to a new clinical project after the initial special attention and funding go away?

options.A: Performance often slips back to old habits
options.B: Staff automatically continue the practice forever
options.C: The hospital board shuts down the entire unit
options.D: Patient satisfaction drops to zero immediately

explanation: Without active efforts to sustain change, wards frequently slide back into their previous routines once the novelty and extra support fade. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h1)

question: Clinic records show few malaria cases, but local medicine vendors report selling lots of malaria drugs daily. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the clinic staff to the ministry for failing to do their jobs
options.B: Use community-based data collection like household surveys to find the real disease burden
options.C: Assume the medicine vendors are lying and close down their shops
options.D: Conclude that malaria has been completely eradicated in that area

explanation: Not everyone goes to the government clinic first; many buy drugs across the counter. To find the true picture, nurses must look beyond clinic logbooks and talk to the community directly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why is rotating the application site essential when a patient uses transdermal patches?

options.A: To ensure the old patch stays stuck to the body for extra dosing
options.B: To prevent skin irritation, breakdown, and altered drug absorption
options.C: To force the medication to travel through different liver pathways
options.D: To stop the patient from forgetting where the patch was placed last week

explanation: Applying patches to the exact same spot repeatedly damages the skin barrier and can change how effectively the drug absorbs into the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: A public health nurse visits a crowded urban settlement to improve sanitation and teach hygiene. Whose historical footsteps is this nurse following?

options.A: A medieval monk
options.B: A hospital surgical specialist
options.C: An ancient herbalist
options.D: Lillian Wald

explanation: Lillian Wald is a legend in public health! She took nursing straight into busy neighborhoods to tackle health and social needs together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why is proper handling and safe transport of laboratory specimens crucial during an outbreak?

options.A: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements in the hospital
options.B: To ensure the laboratory results are ready within five minutes
options.C: To prevent accidental exposure of staff and sample contamination
options.D: To keep the cost of running diagnostic tests as low as possible

explanation: Infectious samples carry live pathogens that can infect handlers or ruin the test if mishandled or contaminated along the way. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why are individuals with pre-existing mental health conditions especially vulnerable during disasters?

options.A: They are completely immune to physical injuries
options.B: Disasters automatically cure their psychiatric symptoms
options.C: Their usual support systems and medication routines are often disrupted
options.D: Emergency workers always prioritize them over everyone else

explanation: When clinics close, pharmacies run out of stock, and daily structures collapse, stable mental health conditions can quickly deteriorate. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is a direct benefit of using research-backed repositioning schedules on the ward?

options.A: An increase in daily patient discharge rates
options.B: A reduction in hospital-acquired pressure ulcers
options.C: Fewer mandatory shifts for junior nurses
options.D: Lower hospital electricity and utility bills

explanation: You got it! Studies on skin care clearly show that turning patients on a structured schedule keeps their skin safe and prevents painful bedsores. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T4#GNS217_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which bacteria is the main cause of typhoid fever?

options.A: Vibrio cholerae
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Shigella dysenteriae
options.D: Salmonella typhi

explanation: You got it! Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. It's a classic organism you'll see often in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h1)

question: Which of these is a must-have element for any true community?

options.A: A modern tertiary care hospital within walking distance
options.B: A shared identity and feeling of belonging among people
options.C: A paved road network connecting all residential homes
options.D: An elected political representative in the national parliament

explanation: A community isn't just buildings and streets—it's the people! A shared sense of connection and belonging is what truly brings a community to life. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h2)

question: Why is time considered so critical when dealing with emergency medical conditions?

options.A: Hospital regulations require fast bed turnover
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for slow care
options.C: Doctors refuse to see patients who wait too long
options.D: Delays can lead to rapid deterioration and death

explanation: In critical emergencies, minutes matter because a failing body system quickly causes permanent harm or death if not supported. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do we bundle maternal and neonatal health services together?

options.A: Midwives only work during the first week after delivery
options.B: It is cheaper for hospitals to buy medications in bulk
options.C: Newborns require the exact same medical treatments as adults
options.D: The health and survival of the mother and baby are directly linked

explanation: Spot on! Mum and baby are a team. Treating them together ensures nothing gets missed during these crucial early stages. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T005#GNS226_U1_T005_h1)

question: What is the main reason nurses use hypothesis testing in research?

options.A: To prove that personal clinical opinions are always correct
options.B: To increase the financial cost of operating a hospital ward
options.C: To evaluate if observed data differences are real or due to chance
options.D: To eliminate the need for collecting patient outcome data

explanation: Great job thinking like a researcher! Hypothesis testing simply uses math to check if what we see in a study is a true effect or just random luck. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T15#GNS217_U4_T15_h1)

question: Which event officially marks day one of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The cessation of progesterone production
options.B: The release of a mature egg
options.C: The thickening of the uterine wall
options.D: The start of menstrual bleeding

explanation: You've got this! Day one of the cycle always starts on the very first day that bleeding begins. Think of it as the official reset button for the cycle. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h1)

question: You are getting ready to change a surgical wound dressing on a patient's kitchen table. What action shows proper technique?

options.A: Spraying the entire wooden kitchen table with surgical disinfectant
options.B: Placing a clean waterproof barrier underneath the sterile supplies
options.C: Performing the procedure without gloves since it is a home setting
options.D: Asking the family to clear all furniture out of the room completely

explanation: Brilliant! Laying down a clean waterproof barrier creates a safe zone for your sterile equipment, protecting it from ordinary household tables. You're thinking like a pro! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is a baseline neurological assessment important for a patient admitted with a head injury?

options.A: To detect subtle changes in status before major complications occur
options.B: To replace the need for physician examinations
options.C: To eliminate the need for ongoing vital sign monitoring
options.D: To diagnose the exact microscopic cellular damage present

explanation: Comparing current neurological findings to an initial baseline helps nurses catch early signs of worsening brain swelling or bleeding. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h8)

question: What is the main reason a nurse schedules serial ultrasounds for a pregnant client with sickle cell disease?

options.A: To check if the maternal pelvis is widening properly
options.B: To measure the exact volume of maternal amniotic fluid daily
options.C: To determine the exact genetic subtype of the fetus
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for fetal anemia

explanation: You're doing great! Regular scans help us check how well the baby is growing and keep an eye out for fetal anemia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h3)

question: Which of these behaviors is a classic example of a checking compulsion?

options.A: Washing the hands with soap for over an hour after touching a doorknob
options.B: Arranging clothing items in strict color-coded order inside a closet
options.C: Repeatedly verifying that the house doors are locked before sleeping
options.D: Silently repeating a specific religious phrase to undo a bad thought

explanation: Well done! Checking means going back over and over again to make sure things like locks or appliances are secure, just to feel safe. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T7#GNS314_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which physical item should the nurse inspect to evaluate medication adherence at home?

options.A: The electrical sockets for signs of dangerous overloading
options.B: The pill bottles or containers to check remaining doses
options.C: The family photo albums on the living room shelves
options.D: The kitchen trash can for discarded food wrappers

explanation: Inspecting medication packaging helps verify whether the client is actually taking their prescribed drugs on schedule. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h3)

question: What do we call the long, multi-celled structure formed when individual muscle-building cells (myoblasts) fuse together?

options.A: Myotube
options.B: Myofibril
options.C: Sarcomere
options.D: Sarcolemma

explanation: When myoblasts join forces, they form a tube-like structure called a myotube before maturing into full muscle fibers. You are mastering the vocabulary! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why are nurses considered the frontline of patient safety in a hospital?

options.A: Because they perform all the laboratory and pharmacy tests
options.B: Because they write all the medical and surgical treatment policies
options.C: Because they hold the legal responsibility for hospital finances
options.D: Because they spend the most continuous time at the patient's bedside

explanation: Because nurses are constantly with patients, they are in the best position to spot early signs of trouble and catch errors. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h6)

question: What measure helps nurses see the actual size or practical importance of a treatment's effect?

options.A: Sample variance
options.B: Effect size
options.C: P-value
options.D: Null hypothesis

explanation: That's correct! Effect size tells you the actual magnitude of the change, helping you decide if the treatment is powerful enough to matter at the bedside. Great job! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h8)

question: Why do educators evaluate a learning activity after you've completed it?

options.A: To increase the number of hours students spend writing essays
options.B: To calculate the total financial budget spent on hospital equipment
options.C: To determine if the activity actually helped students achieve competence
options.D: To decide which students should be expelled from the nursing program

explanation: Evaluating the lesson helps instructors see if the teaching method actually worked for you. [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is an objective measurement nurses use during a nutritional assessment?

options.A: How many meals the patient ate as a child
options.B: The patient's favorite cultural food dishes
options.C: The patient's personal opinion on their appetite
options.D: Body mass index and laboratory blood panels

explanation: Spot on! Objective data means measurable facts—like BMI and lab results—rather than just guessing based on what someone tells you. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a subacute care facility?

options.A: Treating minor outpatient ailments and routine infections
options.B: Managing acute life-threatening surgical emergencies
options.C: Providing short-term rehabilitation and medical management
options.D: Offering permanent residential care for healthy elders

explanation: Spot on! Subacute care bridges the gap between the busy hospital ward and home, giving patients targeted rehab and recovery support. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why must a researcher conduct a literature review early in the process?

options.A: To decide which nurses will be punished for mistakes
options.B: To see what is already known and avoid repeating past work
options.C: To find patients willing to participate in the study
options.D: To determine the exact financial cost of the hospital

explanation: Reading prior studies prevents wasting time on questions that have already been answered thoroughly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why does the foetal circulatory system bypass the lungs?

options.A: The heart pumps too slowly to reach the chest
options.B: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not oxygenate blood yet
options.C: The lungs are too small to receive blood flow
options.D: Oxygen is only needed in the lower body

question: How does a tension pneumothorax cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure?

options.A: Trapped chest air compresses the heart and large blood vessels, reducing blood return
options.B: The patient stops breathing entirely due to complete paralysis of the diaphragm
options.C: Air travels directly into the bloodstream and dissolves all red blood cells
options.D: Fluid fills the lung tissue and drowns the patient from the inside out

question: Which stage of dementia usually lasts the longest and is known for noticeable confusion and wandering?

options.A: Pre-clinical stage
options.B: Early stage
options.C: Middle stage
options.D: Late stage

explanation: The middle stage is typically the longest. It brings clear behavioral changes, like wandering and needing help with daily tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why can waiting for a drop in blood pressure be a sneaky and dangerous way to spot early postpartum bleeding?

options.A: Pregnancy blood volume increases so much that a woman can lose a lot of blood before her BP drops.
options.B: Low blood pressure is completely normal during the first week after birth.
options.C: Postpartum mothers naturally have very high baseline blood pressures.
options.D: Hospital blood pressure machines are almost always inaccurate.

explanation: Because a pregnant woman's body adapts by holding more blood volume, she can lose a dangerous amount before her vital signs suddenly crash. Always watch the bleeding and clinical signs, not just the BP monitor! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h3)

question: How long should patients wait at the clinic after getting an immunization?

options.A: At least 15 minutes
options.B: Exactly two hours
options.C: Until the end of the market day
options.D: No waiting time is required

explanation: That 15-minute window is a crucial safety check just in case a rare allergic reaction pops up right away. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h5)

question: What is the main difference between mechanical and biological vector transmission?

options.A: Biological vectors allow pathogens to develop inside their bodies, while mechanical vectors just carry them externally.
options.B: Biological vectors are always microscopic, while mechanical vectors are visible to the naked eye.
options.C: Mechanical vectors inject venom, while biological vectors only transmit viruses.
options.D: Mechanical vectors bite humans, while biological vectors only land on animal skin.

explanation: You've got this! Biological means the germ actually grows and develops inside the bug before spreading, while mechanical is just an external piggyback ride. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why is it important to clearly define the scope of a community health assessment?

options.A: It shortens the nursing shift schedule for the week
options.B: It eliminates the need to talk to community members
options.C: It guarantees that zero diseases will occur in the area
options.D: It keeps the assessment focused on specific health problems

explanation: Communities have many needs, but trying to fix everything at once can overwhelm your team. Setting a clear scope helps you stay focused and realistic! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h1)

question: How many core elements make up the standard post-abortion care framework?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Three
options.C: Seven
options.D: Five

explanation: You got it! The standard PAC framework is built on five key elements that guide clinical care and community support. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h2)

question: Which type of heat therapy is known to sink deeper into the patient's body tissues?

options.A: Infrared light alone
options.B: Ambient room air
options.C: Moist heat
options.D: Dry heat

explanation: Moisture is a fantastic conductor! Moist heat travels much deeper into stiff, tight muscles than dry heat ever could. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h4)

question: When does tertiary prevention come into play during the course of an illness?

options.C: After disease and complications have already occurred
options.D: When conducting mass screening tests for healthy adults

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in when a disease is already established, focusing on helping the patient recover and manage life. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T17#GNS313_U1_T17_h5)

question: In extended family systems, why do relatives often encourage couples to have many children?

options.A: To stop neighbors from gossiping
options.B: To reduce the cost of buying school uniforms
options.C: To qualify for free electricity vouchers
options.D: To secure lineage strength and farm labor

question: Why is promoting local Nigerian foods better than relying on foreign supplements for community health?

options.A: Local foods have zero carbohydrates and eliminate all diseases
options.B: Local foods are affordable, culturally acceptable, and readily available
options.C: Local foods never spoil even without refrigeration
options.D: Imported supplements are always illegal to prescribe in clinics

explanation: Using familiar, accessible foodstuffs empowers families to eat well long-term without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T005#GNS227_U1_T005_h8)

question: A nutrient crosses the intestinal lining with the help of a carrier protein, moving down its concentration gradient without using ATP. What is this called?

options.C: Simple diffusion
options.D: Active transport

question: Why do nurse researchers set up a conceptual framework before collecting data?

options.A: To replace the need for a formal literature review
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of conducting the study
options.C: To guarantee that the study gets published immediately
options.D: To make sense of complex human experiences and guide the inquiry

explanation: Research can get messy! A good framework helps you organize your thoughts and makes sure you look at all the important parts of a tricky problem. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h1)

question: You just finished charting on a ward computer. What is the most critical action to take right after?

options.B: Turn off the computer monitor screen power
options.C: Print a physical copy of the screen for the desk
options.D: Log out of the computer session completely

question: What is the primary target group for public or community-funded nurseries?

options.A: Children who have already graduated from primary school
options.B: Low-income families and vulnerable populations who need subsidized support
options.C: Exclusively infants who require long-term neonatal intensive care
options.D: Only high-earning corporate executives seeking elite private tutors

explanation: Public and community nurseries are usually subsidized by governments or NGOs to ensure affordable childcare access for families with limited resources. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h2)

question: A clinic gets a large free donation of malaria drugs. To best support the long-term DRF, what should management do?

options.A: Dispense them properly and capture revenue or track stock to build replacement reserves
options.B: Give all the donated medicines away for free without keeping any pharmacy records
options.C: Sell the donated items to private retail pharmacies for personal staff profit
options.D: Hide the drugs in a secure warehouse and wait for local prices to increase

explanation: Great thinking! Treating donations responsibly and tracking every item helps build a sustainable local stock cushion before the free meds run out. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h5)

question: What does decontamination do for a dirty surgical instrument right after use?

options.A: It achieves absolute sterility without the need for an autoclave machine

options.C: It replaces the need for thorough high-level chemical disinfection
options.D: It permanently alters the metal alloy to prevent future corrosion in storage

explanation: Decontamination is your first line of defense. It washes away heavy dirt so you can handle the tools without risking an infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why must nurses rely on evidence-based practice when discussing complementary therapies with patients?

options.A: To ensure the chosen therapies are genuinely safe and effective
options.B: To force patients to stop using all traditional cultural customs
options.C: Because hospital management fines nurses who mention herbs
options.D: Because scientific journals require annual subscriptions

explanation: Brilliant! Evidence-based practice helps protect our patients from harmful trends and guides them toward truly helpful supportive care. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h6)

question: Why does stopping antibiotics early lead to drug resistance?

options.A: The body becomes immune to the healing power of rest
options.B: Expired medications lose their chemical composition
options.C: Stronger bacteria survive low drug levels and multiply
options.D: Good bacteria in the gut destroy the remaining pills

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early leaves the toughest germs alive, and they multiply to create strains that the drug can no longer kill. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do unsafe injections carry a higher risk than many other medical exposures?

options.A: They always involve contaminated intravenous fluids
options.B: They cause immediate systemic allergic reactions
options.C: They are usually performed by untrained family members
options.D: They introduce pathogens directly past the body's skin barrier

explanation: Normally, our skin and mucous membranes act as strong shields against germs. An injection skips past that natural barrier, sending germs straight into tissue or blood. Brilliant logic to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h1)

question: A nurse gives the wrong dose because two drugs have nearly identical packaging. What is the best system-level response?

options.A: Firing the nurse immediately to warn other staff members
options.B: Redesigning the storage layout and advocating for different packaging
options.C: Telling staff to be more careful without changing anything else
options.D: Requiring all nurses to work double shifts without taking breaks

question: During a lumbar puncture, a patient suddenly moves and straightens their legs. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Administer a dose of emergency pain medication

options.C: Increase the flow rate of the intravenous fluids
options.D: Gently guide the patient back into the curled position and remind them to stay still

question: What is the most effective public health strategy for preventing obstetric fistulae in communities?

options.A: Improving access to skilled birth attendants and emergency obstetric care
options.B: Administering daily vitamin supplements during the third trimester
options.C: Providing free diapers to all women living in rural communities
options.D: Encouraging women to give birth at home without professional assistance

explanation: You nailed it! Getting help quickly during difficult labour prevents the prolonged pressure that causes fistulas. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: What score on the muscle strength grading scale indicates normal strength against full resistance?

options.A: Grade 10
options.B: Grade 1
options.C: Grade 3
options.D: Grade 5

question: What is a very common long-term problem for women who survive an untreated pelvic infection after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Premature menopause

options.C: Gestational diabetes

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a BP of 220/130 mmHg, chest pain, and confusion. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Normal white coat syndrome
options.B: Isolated systolic hypertension
options.C: Hypertensive urgency
options.D: Hypertensive emergency

explanation: Extremely high blood pressure plus signs of brain or heart distress (like confusion and chest pain) makes this a critical medical emergency. You're crushing these clinical scenarios! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is the main benefit of true community participation in health projects?

options.A: Nurses no longer need to visit the community for checkups
options.B: Residents take ownership of the project and ensure its long-term success
options.C: The cost of buying medical equipment drops to zero
options.D: The community becomes entirely independent of any government help

explanation: When the people feel the project belongs to them, they will protect and sustain it long after the nurses pack up and leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h7)

question: Where does the lengthwise growth of a long bone happen?

options.D: Articular capsule

question: How should you clean a patient's skin before giving an injection?

options.B: Applying an antiseptic spray and immediately inserting the needle
options.C: Wiping from the outer edges inward toward the center of the site
options.D: Scrubbing vigorously back and forth with a dry cotton ball

explanation: Always move from clean (center) to less clean (outward) to push germs away. Plus, letting the alcohol dry is what actually kills the microbes! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is an example of resource tracking during a disaster?

options.A: Counting how many hours of sleep nurses got last night
options.B: Interviewing community leaders about past local floods
options.C: Predicting what the weather will look like next month
options.D: Monitoring available hospital beds and oxygen tank supplies

explanation: Resource tracking keeps an active count of vital physical items and space needed to care for incoming patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h5)

question: What do we call learning to fear something simply by watching how other people react to it?

options.A: Reading a medical textbook about anxiety
options.B: Developing a fear directly from a physical injury
options.C: Learning to fear something by watching others react with fear
options.D: Inheriting a phobia gene from a grandparent

explanation: This is observational learning! If a child sees a parent scream at the sight of a lizard, the child might pick up that exact same fear just by watching. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Spraying household furniture with industrial bleach daily
options.B: Keeping all windows tightly closed during visits
options.C: Performing proper and frequent hand hygiene
options.D: Wearing sterile surgical gowns for every home visit

explanation: Good old handwashing and using alcohol rubs remove germs fast, protecting both you and your patient from cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T8#GNS324_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why is teaching workers about toxic gases important in factories and industrial sites?

options.A: It helps workers recognize hidden breathing hazards and use safety gear
options.B: It eliminates the need for any medical staff on site
options.C: It reduces the cost of electricity in factories
options.D: It guarantees that machinery will never break down

explanation: Many toxic gases are invisible. Educating workers helps them spot dangers early and protect themselves with proper ventilation and masks. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h8)

question: On a full blood count lab report, what does the abbreviation MCV stand for?

options.A: Minimum capillary vessel
options.B: Measured cellular viscosity
options.C: Mean corpuscular volume
options.D: Maximum clotting velocity

explanation: MCV tells us the average size of the red blood cells. It's super helpful for figuring out what kind of anaemia a patient has! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h3)

question: How does a glucometer turn a drop of blood into a number on the screen?

options.A: By taking a photo of the blood drop
options.B: By sensing the skin temperature of the finger
options.C: By measuring the electrical current from a chemical reaction
options.D: By weighing the plastic strip

explanation: When blood hits the strip, a tiny electrical current is produced. The meter reads this current and turns it into the number you see! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h2)

question: Administrative nursing informatics is primarily used for which of the following tasks?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications directly to patients
options.B: Managing staffing schedules, budgets, and operational metrics
options.C: Designing interactive smartphone apps for general public use
options.D: Conducting laboratory experiments on cellular disease models

explanation: Nurse leaders use administrative tools to oversee hospital operations, staffing levels, and financial or quality metrics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h3)

question: As a nurse, what crucial counseling point must you share with a client choosing natural family planning?

options.A: The calendar method works best for women with unpredictable cycles
options.B: Basal body temperature can replace barrier methods for infection control
options.C: These methods do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Charting must be done only once a week to prevent stress

explanation: Always remind patients: natural family planning only helps with birth control. It offers zero protection against STIs—condoms are still needed for that! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h5)

question: How is menopause officially diagnosed in a patient?

options.A: Surgical removal of the fallopian tubes
options.B: A sudden spike in body temperature
options.C: Complete stop of pituitary hormones
options.D: Twelve straight months without a menstrual period

explanation: You got it! Clinicians look back and confirm menopause once a woman has gone a full 12 months without any bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main reason we help patients work on their range of motion during rehab?

options.A: To increase the resting blood pressure of the client
options.B: To permanently numb the nerves surrounding a painful joint
options.C: To double the physical size of damaged muscle fibers
options.D: To prevent joint contractures and keep tissues flexible

explanation: Spot on! Moving those joints gently stops them from freezing up or getting stiff so the patient can keep their flexibility. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h2)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water
options.B: Fill out an incident report form for the manager
options.C: Squeeze the finger tightly to push out old blood
options.D: Apply an antiseptic iodine ointment and a bandage

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral or bacterial load introduced at the puncture site before it enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why do community nurses rely heavily on basic anthropometric tools like measuring tapes?

options.A: Advanced hospital equipment is always brought to the field
options.B: Blood tests are illegal outside of licensed hospitals
options.C: Patients prefer tape measurements over physical examinations
options.D: They allow quick screening of large populations in remote areas

explanation: Remote clinics lack heavy laboratory equipment, so nurses use simple tools to screen many people efficiently. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h1)

question: What do altmetrics mainly track when measuring how far a research study has traveled?

options.A: How many patients refuse to take their prescribed pills
options.B: Social media mentions and online news coverage
options.C: The exact cost of printing paper hospital posters
options.D: The number of physical books sold in university shops

explanation: You got it! Altmetrics look at online buzz, like shares on social media, blogs, and news platforms. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h7)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.B: Quarantine is permanent, while isolation lasts for only a few hours
options.C: Isolation is for animals, while quarantine is strictly for human patients
options.D: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation only uses physical barriers

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation keeps already sick people away from others. Quarantine keeps healthy people who were exposed to a germ apart, just in case they develop symptoms later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h6)

question: In Vroom's expectancy theory, what does 'expectancy' actually mean?

options.A: The fear of being punished for a clinical error
options.B: The financial value attached to a year-end bonus
options.C: The belief that effort will lead to successful performance
options.D: The strict rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Correct! Expectancy is your personal belief that if you work hard, you will actually succeed at the task. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why does your body slow down digestion when the sympathetic system kicks in?

options.A: To cool down internal body organs during sudden exertion
options.B: To allow the liver to store extra glucose for later use
options.C: To redirect blood and energy toward muscles needed for survival
options.D: To prevent the stomach from producing excess digestive acid

explanation: When you need to run or fight, your body sends blood where it matters most—your muscles and heart! Digestion can wait for a calmer moment. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T30#GNS211_U3_T30_h1)

question: Why must you use the same data collection tools throughout a longitudinal study?

options.A: To make sure the research assistants do not have to work very hard
options.B: To ensure that measured changes are real and not caused by changing the measurement tool
options.C: To comply with rules about destroying old medical records
options.D: To keep the total budget of the research project at zero

explanation: Exactly! If you change your measuring instrument, you won't know if patient scores changed because their health changed or simply because the tool was different. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why might a nurse face pushback when trying to bring about changes in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Government laws strictly forbid nurses from speaking in public
options.B: Patients always oppose changes that improve their health outcomes
options.C: Medical doctors are legally required to stop all nursing activities
options.D: Superiors may feel threatened or prefer to maintain corrupt or comfortable habits

explanation: You nailed it! People in charge sometimes resist change because they are used to old habits or feel exposed when a nurse points out system failures. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h8)

question: What is the main goal of routine health check-ups in the workplace?

options.A: To determine the exact monthly salary of each employee
options.B: To help the company fire workers who take sick leave
options.C: To diagnose unrelated personal illnesses like childhood malaria
options.D: To detect early signs of work-related illness before permanent damage occurs

explanation: Early detection is key in nursing! Routine checks catch small health issues early on, stopping them from turning into major, long-term illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h5)

question: What key element is missing from a vague aim statement like 'we will improve patient safety'?

options.A: Detailed medical diagnoses for every patient
options.B: A complete history of past nursing errors
options.C: The signatures of the hospital board of directors
options.D: Specific targets, a timeline, and the target patient group

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Without knowing how much change, by when, and for whom, a team can't measure success. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why is building trust so important when giving nutrition advice to outpatients?

options.A: Nurses must legally enforce strict hospital meal schedules
options.B: Clients have autonomy over their daily food choices at home
options.C: Outpatients only eat when supervised by a healthcare provider
options.D: Dietary plans rarely change once the client leaves the clinic

explanation: Spot on! Since outpatients control what they eat at home, having a trusting relationship makes them much more likely to follow your advice. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h1)

question: What is the normal pH range of the skin's protective acid mantle?
explanation: Well done! A slightly acidic pH between 4.5 and 5.5 makes it hard for harmful bacteria and fungi to grow on us. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is an obstetric fistula?

options.A: A sudden infection of the ovaries following childbirth
options.B: An abnormal opening between the birth canal and bladder or rectum
options.C: A temporary swelling of the external genitalia
options.D: A complete rupture of the uterine wall during early gestation

explanation: Prolonged pressure during difficult labor cuts off blood supply, creating a hole that leads to constant leaking of urine or stool. It's a heartbreaking condition we work hard to prevent and care for. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why do esophageal varices develop in patients with portal hypertension?

options.A: Blood backs up and forces open alternative collateral channels connecting portal and systemic veins
options.B: High stomach acid burns through the protective mucosal barrier of the esophagus
options.C: Swallowed food scraps scrape against the lining of the stomach and damage blood vessels
options.D: The liver releases excess clotting factors that clog small blood vessels near the throat

explanation: When the main gateway to the liver is blocked by high pressure, blood looks for alternative escape routes. It forces open smaller, fragile veins around the esophagus, causing them to bulge out like balloons (varices). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h4)

question: What key tip should you give a patient about finishing their prescribed antiparasitic pills?

options.A: Share the remaining medication with family members who feel itchy
options.B: Complete the entire course of medication even if symptoms disappear
options.C: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill on time
options.D: Stop taking the pills as soon as your stomach starts feeling better

explanation: Even if the patient starts feeling 100% better, remind them to finish every single pill. Stopping early means some parasites might still be hiding out ready to cause a comeback! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h7)

question: A ward manager notices staff are burning out and making mistakes on night shifts due to bad scheduling. What should be done first?

options.A: Stop holding shift handovers to save working time
options.B: Punish the nurses for making clinical errors during the night
options.C: Increase the number of patients assigned to each nurse
options.D: Redesign the roster to balance shift distribution and staff skill mix

explanation: Brilliant choice! When scheduling causes fatigue and errors, the best fix is to address the root problem by making a fairer, safer roster. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h7)

question: Why do nurses need to work closely with logistics officers during an emergency?

options.A: To negotiate international trade agreements for pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.B: To ensure fragile medical supplies like vaccines remain viable during transport
options.C: To drive heavy transport trucks through blocked disaster zones
options.D: To manage the financial bank accounts of the Ministry of Health

explanation: Nurses know how delicate items like vaccines are, so their guidance helps logistics officers transport them safely. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T8#GNS315_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why do pregnant women have a significantly higher nutritional requirement for specific minerals like iron?

options.A: To support expanding blood volume and fetal growth
options.B: To completely prevent gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To replace electrolytes lost through morning sickness
options.D: To cure pre-existing chronic bone infections

explanation: Pregnancy causes a major increase in blood volume and requires extra nutrients to support the developing fetus and placenta. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why are traditional media like village drama troupes and town criers so effective in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: They use familiar cultural formats that local people easily relate to
options.B: They require expensive electricity and satellite dishes
options.C: They are the only legal way to share health messages
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for trained nurses

explanation: Exactly! When you meet people through their own cultural practices like drama and town criers, they naturally tune in and trust the message. Great public health intuition! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why does the foramen ovale close immediately after birth?

options.A: The umbilical cord clamp pushes blood into the heart chambers

options.C: Muscles in the atrial wall contract and seal the hole shut
options.D: Pressure in the left atrium becomes higher than the right atrium

explanation: Blood returning from the newly opened lungs raises left atrial pressure, pushing the flap of the foramen ovale closed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: What is the plastic sheet in a delivery kit used for?

options.A: To wrap the newborn to keep it warm
options.B: To tie off the umbilical cord securely
options.C: To provide a clean surface for delivery
options.D: To clean the hands of the birth attendant

explanation: The plastic sheet is laid down to protect the mother from laying on contaminated ground or unhygienic flooring. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water over an alcohol-based hand rub?

options.A: When you are in a rush between medication rounds
options.B: Every time you enter a clean patient room
options.C: Before taking the blood pressure of a healthy adult
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and water physically wash away visible dirt, organic material, and certain tough spores that alcohol rubs cannot destroy effectively. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h4)

question: What usually happens to the demand for routine healthcare when out-of-pocket prices go up?

options.A: Demand increases
options.B: Demand fluctuates randomly every day
options.C: Demand remains completely unchanged
options.D: Demand decreases

explanation: Makes total sense, right? When treatment becomes too expensive, fewer people are able or willing to go for routine check-ups. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is a mandatory requirement for any injectable (parenteral) drug preparation?

options.A: It must contain a high concentration of added sugar
options.B: It must be mixed with thick oil to slow down absorption
options.C: It must be completely sterile and free from pyrogens
options.D: It must have a strong, pleasant artificial fruit flavour

explanation: Injectable drugs bypass your patient's natural digestive defenses, so they must be completely sterile to prevent severe infections and dangerous fevers. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which management system do hospitals use during emergencies to keep a clear chain of command?

options.A: The Hospital Budget Allocation Matrix
options.B: The Nursing Process Evaluation Model
options.C: The Incident Command System (ICS)
options.D: The Primary Health Care Algorithm

explanation: In an emergency, everyone needs to know who is in charge. The ICS provides a clear, organized leadership structure so rescue efforts run smoothly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the job of dense bodies inside smooth muscle cells?

options.A: They store calcium ions before contraction
options.B: They serve as anchors for actin and myosin filaments
options.C: They transmit electrical signals directly between cells
options.D: They produce the chemical energy needed for relaxation

explanation: Dense bodies act like tiny hitching posts inside the cell, giving the muscle fibers something firm to pull against when it's time to squeeze. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h2)

question: Why are flashing lights and visual alert systems helpful for patients with severe hearing loss?

options.A: They provide visual warnings for home safety hazards that sounds might miss
options.B: Flashing lights help regenerate damaged hair cells inside the inner ear
options.C: They replace the need for regular hearing aid battery replacements
options.D: Bright lights automatically adjust the volume of household televisions

explanation: Brilliant! Since they might miss audio cues, flashing lights for doorbells or smoke alarms help keep them safe at home. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main reason for doing a medication review during a home visit after a hospital discharge?

options.A: To throw away all old medications so the client can buy new ones
options.B: To let the family decide which pills the client should swallow
options.C: To increase the total number of daily prescription drugs
options.D: To compare hospital discharge orders with what the client is actually taking

explanation: Spot on! Medication reconciliation clears up any confusion so the client takes the exact right drugs safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing a Job Safety Analysis (JSA)?

options.A: Conducting routine blood pressure checks on factory workers
options.B: Calculating the monthly profit margin of an industrial plant
options.C: Breaking down a task step-by-step to spot hidden dangers
options.D: Measuring the exact decibel levels of factory machinery

explanation: A JSA looks at every little step of a job to catch safety risks before someone gets hurt. Teamwork makes safety work! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T6#GNS225_U7_T6_h5)

question: When should a primary health nurse initiate an upward referral for a psychiatric client?

options.A: As soon as the client's symptoms begin to improve on standard medication
options.B: Whenever the client misses a single routine clinic appointment
options.C: When the client develops severe psychosis or active suicidal ideation beyond local management
options.D: When the local clinic runs out of printed health education leaflets

explanation: If a patient's condition becomes too severe for the local clinic to safely handle—like active suicidal thoughts—it's time for an upward referral to specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the main perk of using an arterial line in an intensive care unit?

options.A: Checking oxygen levels without using a finger probe
options.B: Automatic injection of emergency drugs
options.C: Measuring exhaled carbon dioxide
options.D: Continuous, beat-by-beat blood pressure measurement

explanation: An arterial line sits right inside the artery to give a real-time, exact blood pressure reading with every single heartbeat. Perfect for critical care! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why is clear, open communication during shift handovers so vital in team nursing?

options.A: It makes the shift last longer than necessary
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not speak to nurses
options.C: It prevents fragmented care and catches clinical changes early
options.D: It stops patients from asking questions about their health

explanation: Exactly! Sharing vital updates ensures everyone is on the same page regarding patient status, which keeps our patients safe from errors. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why does eating fat cause sharp tummy pain for someone with an inflamed gallbladder (cholecystitis)?

options.A: Undigested fats ferment quickly and create dangerous gas pockets
options.B: The liver stops producing blood proteins when fats enter the duodenum
options.C: Fat stimulates the gallbladder to contract against an inflamed or blocked tract
options.D: Lipids chemically burn the delicate lining of the stomach wall

explanation: Well done! When fat enters the gut, the gallbladder squeezes to release bile. If it's inflamed or blocked, that squeezing hurts! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T006#GNS227_U6_T006_h2)

question: Why are clinical nurse champions so effective at spreading new practices on a busy ward?

options.A: They have the legal power to fire staff who break rules
options.B: They write all hospital policies without management approval
options.C: They spend all working hours reading international journals
options.D: They are respected peers who mentor and encourage other staff

explanation: You're right on track! Nurse champions lead from within the team, making it much easier and friendlier for colleagues to embrace new habits. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of these choices is a MAJOR safety violation when handling hospital equipment?

options.A: Checking for frayed electrical cords
options.B: Obtaining informed consent from the patient
options.C: Skipping equipment cleaning to save time
options.D: Ensuring proper disinfection between patients

explanation: Never skip cleaning! Proper maintenance and disinfection protect patients from nasty infections and keep equipment running smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is a key ethical rule during a virtual nursing consultation?

options.A: Avoiding the need for formal informed consent
options.B: Sharing the patient's phone number with local vendors
options.C: Recording the session to post on public social media
options.D: Protecting patient confidentiality and privacy

explanation: Just like in the hospital ward, a patient's privacy remains sacred during online and phone consultations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: A student wants to study 'hospital stress'. Which option is a well-focused, realistic research topic?

options.A: Reviewing the history of global healthcare systems
options.B: Comparing the salaries of all hospital workers worldwide
options.C: Assessing night-shift burnout among intensive care unit nurses
options.D: Finding out why people get stressed in all buildings

explanation: Great research topics are narrow and specific! Focusing on a particular group (ICU nurses) and issue (night-shift burnout) makes your study much easier to manage. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h2)

question: What exactly do we mean by a "food myth" in healthcare?

options.A: A dietary belief that lacks scientific support
options.B: An official government nutrition guideline
options.C: A modern recipe created by clinical dietitians
options.D: A strict medical prescription for a disease

explanation: Food myths are unverified ideas about what food does to the body, passed along without scientific proof. Don't worry, once you spot them in clinical practice, they become much easier to address! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h1)

question: How can a clinic best handle scheduling barriers for teenagers who are still in school?

options.A: By refusing service to anyone under eighteen years old
options.B: By forcing students to drop out of school to attend clinics
options.C: By closing down clinics entirely during exam weeks
options.D: By offering flexible operating hours and weekend services

explanation: Flexibility is key! Offering weekend or after-school hours ensures students don't have to choose between their education and their health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h5)

question: What is a major feature of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in the health sector?

options.A: They are fully funded by compulsory federal taxes
options.B: They only provide care within major urban teaching hospitals
options.C: They operate independently from direct government control
options.D: They are legally required to employ only government civil servants

explanation: NGOs run as private, independent bodies separate from state or federal government management, even though they often partner with the government. [learn more](GST322_U4_T12#GST322_U4_T12_h2)

question: Which tool is used most often during pregnancy to check for physical birth defects?

options.A: A complete blood count
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Ultrasonography
options.D: An electrocardiogram

explanation: Obstetric ultrasound is safe, painless, and lets doctors peek inside the womb to see how baby is growing! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h5)

question: How do safe youth clubs and recreational activities help prevent substance abuse?

options.A: By providing legal access to prescription medications
options.B: By completely eliminating all life challenges and pressures
options.C: By forcing adolescents to study chemistry all day
options.D: By giving teenagers healthy ways to manage stress and stay engaged

explanation: Spot on! Fun, positive activities keep youth active, boost their self-esteem, and give them great outlets to handle stress instead of turning to drugs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why must nurses handle EENT physical assessments with extra care?

options.A: Patients are usually asleep under general anesthesia
options.B: Infection control rules don't apply to the face
options.C: These body parts have no nerves and cannot feel pain
options.D: The body parts are delicate, tightly packed, and connected

explanation: EENT organs have fragile tissues and important sensory spots, so you always want to use gentle hands and proper tools during exams. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why should you never use both hands to recap a used needle?

options.A: It bends the needle tip and makes the injection painful
options.B: It drastically increases the risk of an accidental needle-stick injury
options.C: It violates hospital policies regarding medication waste disposal
options.D: It takes too much time during a busy medication round

explanation: Using two hands to recap makes it way too easy to miss the cap and puncture your own finger. Safety first—keep that hand away from the sharp end! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main use of an action plan when implementing a program?

options.A: Calculating the total profit generated by the health facility
options.B: Writing the final academic research paper about the project
options.C: Breaking high-level goals down into specific daily and weekly tasks
options.D: Punishing staff members who fail to meet unrealistic deadlines

explanation: An action plan takes big, scary project goals and chops them into bite-sized daily and weekly steps that are easy to manage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is the very first step in the community mobilisation process?

options.A: Building a permanent hospital
options.B: Evaluating project funds
options.C: Mass immunisation
options.D: Entry and sensitization

explanation: Before doing anything else, health workers must properly introduce themselves and gain entry through appropriate community channels. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which nursing action is best for stopping parasites from spreading through a community?

options.A: Ordering immediate major surgery for all children
options.B: Restricting patients from drinking clean tap water
options.C: Teaching proper handwashing and personal hygiene
options.D: Isolating infected patients in private hospital rooms

explanation: Good community education on handwashing and safe food habits cuts right through the fecal-oral chain of transmission. Excellent! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which factor is part of an environmental safety assessment for a client with balance problems?

options.A: Checking for loose rugs, poor lighting, and stairs
options.B: Checking the color of the paint on the bedroom walls
options.C: Counting the number of chairs in the living room
options.D: Measuring the room temperature and humidity levels

explanation: Environmental checks focus on removing physical hazards like tripping risks to prevent falls at home. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h7)

question: What exactly is a nerve pathway?

options.A: An open space where hormones travel through the bloodstream
options.B: A blood vessel supplying oxygen directly to the brain cells

question: Why is it risky to reuse old prescription drugs for a new sickness?

question: When a nursing manager has to settle a dispute between two departments, what should be their main goal?

question: What is the most practical skill a nurse should teach a patient to maintain a low-fat diet at home?

question: Why is checking the patient's platelet count important before a lumbar puncture?

question: What is the main job of an enzyme in the body?

options.C: Grief only happens after sudden trauma, while bereavement occurs exclusively in chronic illnesses
options.D: Grief involves physical pain only, while bereavement involves purely spiritual distress

explanation: Exactly right! Grief is the heavy emotional feeling inside, while bereavement is the broader period of experiencing the loss of someone close to you. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing action when managing an outbreak using incubation data?

options.A: Prescribing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every community resident
options.B: Calculating the probable exposure date for sick patients
options.C: Stocking adequate testing supplies for anticipated surges
options.D: Educating exposed contacts on why they need to monitor symptoms

explanation: Spot on! Giving out unnecessary antibiotics causes drug resistance. Nurses focus on tracking, educating, and supporting the community instead. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is helping clients connect with their community an important part of day and night hospital care?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any ongoing medication
options.B: It reduces stigma and helps clients function within their social environment
options.C: It ensures patients never have to return to their families
options.D: It allows the hospital to discharge staff and save money

explanation: You got it! Keeping clients connected to their communities builds acceptance and supports long-term recovery. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do many traditional taboos give the best pieces of meat to adult males instead of children?

options.A: Cultural hierarchy assigns priority foods to providers and leaders
options.B: Adult males require more physical energy to farm and hunt
options.C: Children's digestive systems cannot process animal protein
options.D: Meat spoils faster when eaten by younger family members

explanation: Traditional power structures often dictate that heads of households and male breadwinners receive the most prized food items first. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h4)

question: Why is colchicine sometimes given along with NSAIDs to treat pericarditis?

options.A: To dissolve existing blood clots inside the heart chambers
options.B: To destroy resistant bacterial strains in the bloodstream
options.C: To permanently lower the patient's resting heart rate
options.D: To help prevent future episodes of the condition from returning

explanation: Colchicine is a helpful anti-inflammatory medicine added to treatment to stop pericarditis from coming back to trouble the patient again. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h5)

question: In the '5 As' smoking cessation framework, which step means checking if a patient uses tobacco during every clinic visit?

options.A: Assess
options.B: Advise
options.C: Ask
options.D: Arrange

explanation: The 'Ask' step is simply checking and recording whether every patient uses tobacco. Simple, direct, and essential for good nursing care! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h5)

question: What type of tissue does a somatic reflex target?

options.A: Smooth muscle of blood vessels
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Endocrine glands
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Somatic reflexes deal with your voluntary skeletal muscles—the ones that let you move your arms, legs, and body around. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h7)

question: Why do community health nurses look at accidents as things we can prevent rather than just 'bad luck'?

options.A: Because bad luck cannot be studied scientifically
options.B: Because most accidents follow preventable patterns
options.C: Because hospitals profit directly from treating injuries
options.D: Because government policies cause all accidents

explanation: Spotting accidents as preventable events helps us design safety steps that keep our communities safe and injury-free! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T12#GNS313_U3_T12_h1)

question: Why does a failure in cell death (apoptosis) lead to autoimmune disease?

options.A: Bone marrow stops making new white blood cells
options.B: Pathogens are allowed to hide inside dying cells
options.C: Healthy cells die too quickly and release too many nutrients
options.D: Autoreactive lymphocytes survive instead of undergoing programmed cell death

explanation: Normally, rogue immune cells that could attack our body are told to self-destruct. When that fails, these harmful cells stick around and cause trouble. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h2)

question: A nurse wants to study pregnant women nationwide, but she only collects data from patients at her own clinic. What is her clinic patient group called?

options.A: The control population
options.B: The accessible population
options.C: The sampling frame
options.D: The target population

explanation: Exactly! They are your accessible population because they are right there in your clinic, ready and easy for you to reach for your study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T16#GNS224_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which of these is a BIG NO-ROUTINE in infection control during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: Decontaminating room surfaces with chlorine solutions
options.B: Reusing disposable gloves after washing them with ordinary soap
options.C: Limiting the number of staff entering the isolation zone
options.D: Using a trained buddy to watch you remove your PPE

explanation: You got it! Disposable gloves are strictly one-time-use. Never wash and reuse them—safety first! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h6)

question: What do chemical indicator strips placed on a sterile pack actually tell the nurse?

options.A: The autoclave machine is fully repaired and working
options.B: The package was exposed to the required temperature or steam
options.C: The instruments inside have no rust or organic debris
options.D: All bacteria inside the pack are completely dead

explanation: Chemical indicators change color to show heat exposure, but they do not guarantee that the required time or conditions killed all germs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: Which sign is most characteristic of the compensated stage of shock?

options.A: Normal blood pressure maintained by compensatory mechanisms
options.B: Slow, bounding pulse with warm, flushed skin
options.C: Severe drop in blood pressure and clear fluid overload
options.D: Unresponsive patient with zero urine output

explanation: In the compensated stage, the body successfully uses heart rate and blood vessel tightening to keep blood pressure within normal limits. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h2)
